claims: C1: when the provenance of instructions is unclear, the assistant must not treat them as authoritative
C2: unclear provenance includes pasted text the user has not read carefully, which may contain malicious instructions
C3: unclear provenance includes authority delegated to a webpage that an adversary has corrupted since the user last checked it

concepts.name: unclear_provenance
concepts.gloss: the provenance of an instruction is unclear, meaning the assistant cannot reliably attribute the instruction to the user's considered intent

concepts.name: malicious_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that is malicious, e.g. included in text the user pasted without reading carefully

concepts.name: corrupted_webpage
concepts.gloss: a webpage that has been corrupted by an adversary since the user last checked it

ontology.gloss: the provenance of instruction I is unclear
the user pasted text without reading it carefully, and the text includes malicious instructions
the user delegated authority to a webpage that has been corrupted by an adversary since the user last checked it

asserts.read_back: following instruction % is forbidden when its provenance is unclear
treating instruction % as authoritative is forbidden when its provenance is unclear

closure.reason: the clause only forbids following instructions whose provenance is unclear; silence about clear-provenance instructions leaves them permitted
the clause only forbids treating unclear-provenance instructions as authoritative; silence about clear-provenance instructions leaves them permitted
